transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I'm here to help answer any questions you might have about your cataract surgery or your recovery. 

Is there anything you'd like to ask me about?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hi Dora, thanks for taking my call. I do have a few questions. Firstly, when can I start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great! That's a good question. You should avoid any exercise for the first week after your surgery. But after that week, you can go back to light exercise like gardening. So you'd be fine to do some gentle gardening from about a week onwards.

Just avoid anything too strenuous or heavy for about a month after your surgery.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for the advice. My next question is, when can I start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. If you were using eye drops or gel for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

So you should be fine to keep using your dry eye gel as you were before. If you're not sure about the specific timing or have any concerns, it's best to check with your care team.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thanks for that information. I do have another question. I'm very sensitive to bright light. Is that normal?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a common concern. It is normal for your eyes to be a bit sensitive to light as they adjust to your new lenses. 

If it's mild and things just seem brighter than you're used to, we'd recommend wearing sunglasses when you're outside.

However, if you're experiencing significant pain in bright light, or if your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further. In that case, I'd suggest contacting your care team.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: I appreciate the clarification. My last question is, should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
That's a good question. It's quite common for vision to not be completely clear in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

However, I don't have your specific details, so I'm not sure exactly how long it's been since your operation. If your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything is okay.

If you're concerned, it's best to mention it to your care team.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for the reassurance, Dora. I don't have any more questions for now. I really appreciate your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's wonderful! Just to confirm - have all your questions been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, you've addressed all my questions. Thanks again for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! I'm glad I could help. Take care, and all the best with your recovery!

verdict.label: pass
